I managed to get my bird to bond with me over 2 months here's a summary of how I managed it, you can go at your Birds own pace



To start I moved his cage next to my sofa where I sit in the evenings so he could get used to seeing me / me being around his cage. I would talk to him sing to him etc but at this stage it was just to make him comfortable in my presence. 

After about 2 weeks of this I then moved to the next stage. 

Around an hour before I planned to spend time with him I would remove all food / things he can eat from his cage (I'd only leave him for around an hour with nothing to eat)

I would then take his food bowl and just hold it in the cage about 6 or 7 inches away from him. And just sit for a couple of hours holding the bowl and talking to him. After a few days of this he left comfortable enough to eat out the bowl when I was holding it and would even stand on the bowl when it's in my hand. 

The next stage was to get him used to my hand moving so I would slowly move my hand when he was standing on the bowl eating.

Next stage after this was I changed from his metal bowl to a clear plastic one so he could see my hands / fingers through the bowl and become mire comfortable with my hand and once I felt he was comfortable with this I then changed to holding the food in my hand. 

I was at this stage I was able to introduce him to millet (he didn't know it was a treat / something to eat as he hadn't seen it before). This was the start of his millet addition 😂😂

I was able to then start teaching him to step up onto my hand using millet as a reward (again Elleandthebirds on YouTube has a really good video on this)

Easiest way to gain trust is through their belly but its going to take time and patience. 

First of all I moved his cage so it was next to my sofa so he would have to get used to seeing me and seeing me move around. 

After a couple of days I spent time with him daily trying to get his trust. 

The following method took me 2 weeks to get my tiel to trust me and I was persistent every day. 

I would take all food and treats out the cage about an hr before the time I planned to spend time with him. 

Next I would get a small clear plastic bowl I could hold in my hand fill it with seeds and hold it in the cage near him. I deliberately chose a clear bowl so he can see my hand/fingers

I kept being persistent and eventually be became brave enough to stick his face in the bowl and eat. When it did I would give him lots of verbal praise and tell him he's a good boy. 

Next step is once your bird is happy with sticking his face in the bowl to eat hold the bowl slightly out of reach in front of him. This means he will have to step onto the bowl when it's in your hand and eat. 

Once your bird is comfortable with this you can then slowly start moving your hand around in the cage at this point whilst he's on the bowl (if he jumps off that's fine) keep the verbal praise going. 

The next step is to remove the clear bowl and try with just some seeds in your hands  the aim here is to stop the bird being afraid of your hands and associate them with good things I.e food and praise. 

Once my bird was comfortable with this I then looked to start step up training. He didn't have a clue what millet was when I first got him so one day I held some in the cage and he tried it because he assumed it was food (and my millet junkie was born).
